transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CSM) — Amir Zadeh (CTO), Priya Sharma (Lead ML Eng), Tom Rivera (Infra Eng), Sofia (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand Copperpond's constraints for time-to-first-token (TTFT), tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted (PLG self-serve) vs Dedicated or Private deployment, and next steps to run a small benchmark/pilot. Customer emphasized data residency and auditability; also cost sensitivity for production inference.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? We're on a tight 30-45 min window so we'll try to get to the deployment constraints and TTFT.
[00:18] Amir (Copperpond): Hi, Amir here — CTO. Priya is our ML lead, Tom's infra, Sofia product. We're evaluating quick ways to get embeddings + chat generation in our product, like under 2 weeks to prototype.
[00:33] Jon (Redwood SE): Great. Quick note on the agenda: PLG/self-serve quickstart using Redwood API (free credits, token path), and then when Dedicated or Private makes sense — cost vs latency and security tradeoffs. We'll also capture success criteria and stakeholders.
[00:51] Priya (Customer): Our main blocker is we have GDPR customers in EU and also a subset of healthcare partners — so data residency and audit logs are a must. We also need to see p50/p95 latency under load for 20 qps.
[01:05] Tom (Customer): Ops is worried about long-term predictable cost; we don't want surprises with per-token. We're also looking at on-prem possibilities.
[01:16] Lena: Totally. Quick question — is this initially internal prototype or public-facing? That impacts hosting choice.
[01:22] Sofia: Public-facing, limited beta in two markets (US + EU) — low QPS to start but will ramp if success.
[01:30] Jon: Ok. For TTFT, self-serve Redwood API with free credits can get you to first token in hours — create account, API key, drop-in SDKs. The full PLG flow: credits, quickstart notebook, example prompts, and a sample integration for streaming responses.
[01:48] Amir: Hours is great. But how about audit logs and SSO? We need SAML SSO and retention for 365 days or ability to export audit logs.
[01:58] Maya (CSM): We support SSO for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has SSO for Enterprise tiers — we can surface SAML options, and audit logs can be exported. I'll attach the SOC2 and audit doc.
[02:12] Priya: And encryption? KMS? HSM?
[02:16] Jon: For Private deployments you manage KMS/HSM. For Hosted we integrate with cloud KMS and offer customer-managed keys on certain plans — we'll share the KMS matrix. Note: hosted customer-managed keys can add some key-rotation and latency tradeoffs depending on provider.
[02:33] Amir: Makes sense. On cost — you mentioned Dedicated reserved capacity. Is that per-GPU per-hour plus slot commitments? How predictable is it versus per-token?
[02:43] Lena: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — monthly commit for predictable throughput, and you can configure autoscaling with burst capacity. Per-token hosted usage is variable but we provide tools (Optimize) to recommend batching/quantization to control unit economics.
[02:58] Priya: We're especially interested in embedding pipelines (batch) and chat (low-latency). Any guidance on mixing both?
[03:06] Jon: Yes — for embeddings, continuous batching and async jobs on Dedicated gives best cost efficiency. For chat, you tune batch size and KV cache, plus route low-latency requests to nodes pinned for small seq lengths. We can show you sample configs.
[03:24] Sofia: Can you do a short sketch of pilot plan? We have two weeks to get a working prototype and then 2-3 week pilot with customers.
[03:31] Lena: Proposed: Week 0—account setup + free credits quickstart (TTFT: <1 day). Week 1—integrate embeddings + chat with test dataset, run basic evals. Week 2—benchmarks with target QPS and latency; choose Hosted pilot vs Dedicated PoC based on results and security needs.
[03:49] Tom: For the benchmarks, we need to run with our sample corpus and measure 95th pct latencies at 20 QPS and 100 QPS. Is that doable in hosted?
[03:58] Jon: Hosted can run benchmarks but there are noisy neighbor effects at very high QPS; for production-grade stable 95th pct under load we often recommend Dedicated or a private lane. But for evaluation Hosted will give you a good signal. We'll run an apples-to-apples open-model baseline on Dedicated-equivalent hardware for comparison.
[04:20] Priya: You said KV cache earlier — how transparent is that? We have chat sessions that benefit from prefix caching.
[04:26] Jon: KV cache is managed by the runtime. On Dedicated you can control cache retention and which model variants use it. Hosted uses smart prefix caching heuristics; we can show you visibility in the console for cache hit rates.
[04:40] Amir: Ok, two red flags for us: data residency in EU and SSO/audit logs. If Hosted doesn't meet that, we need Private. How fast can Private be stood up?
[04:51] Lena: Private (VPC) typically takes 4–8 weeks depending on networking and approvals; on-prem longer. Dedicated is a middle ground — reserved in a cloud region with isolation guarantees, usually 2–4 weeks. But for proof-of-concept you can use Hosted with contractual assurances and then move to Dedicated once commit is needed.
[05:12] Sofia: Any compliance docs we can review now?
[05:15] Maya: I'll attach SOC 2, ISO summary, our security whitepaper, and the KMS/HSM integration doc. Also sample contracts for a Dedicated commitment.
[05:25] Amir: Good. About pricing — can you give a ballpark for Dedicated monthly commit for our expected peak (100 QPS chat + 1k embeddings/hr)?
[05:34] Lena: Ballpark on a call like this is rough, but for 100 QPS chat you'd likely be in a multi-GPU pool — ballpark thousands to tens of thousands per month depending on quantization and model choice. We'll send a pricing sheet and do a tailored estimate after we see the sample workload.
[05:55] Priya: Model list — do you host open models and do you support quantized variants? We prefer open models for licensing reasons.
[06:02] Jon: Yes, Redwood hosts curated open models, Redwood-verified performance profiles, and we support quantized variants. Optimize will recommend quantization levels and kernel choices for your workload.
[06:16] Amir: Competitors — we've looked at OpenAI for hosted simplicity and Anthropic for chat quality, but integration and cost is a concern. Any differences in SSO and private options?
[06:30] Lena: Main differentiation: Redwood focuses on unified inference across hosted, dedicated, and private — same API and operational tooling. We emphasize observability (token cost breakdowns, per-model dashboards) and rollout controls.
[06:44] Sofia: Ok. Can we also get a sample SLO for latency and an example canary rollout policy? We want to see how Redwood handles model rollbacks on regressions.
[06:54] Jon: Yes — we have built-in A/B and canary tooling, automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll share a sample policy that triggers rollback if p95 increases by 30% on the sample eval set.
[07:12] Priya: On the technical checklist, we need: SSO + RBAC, audit logs export, KMS support, EU data residency option, model version pinning, and ability to run on Dedicated GPUs.
[07:25] Lena: Got it — we'll include a checklist in the follow-up.
[07:30] Amir: Timeline and stakeholders — decision maker is me and CFO for budget, we'll need an SE-led benchmark and legal to review SOC2. If the benchmark looks good, likely Dedicated commit.
[07:45] Maya: Who should we loop in from legal?
[07:48] Amir: I'll share our GA and legal contact after the call.
[07:52] Lena: Cool. Any blockers for starting quickstart today?
[07:56] Priya: We need a legal ok for sharing an anonymized dataset but can scrub PII and send a slice.
[08:02] Tom: Also need an ops contact for network whitelisting if we end up with Dedicated test cluster.
[08:08] Jon: Noted. For the benchmark we'll provide a runbook — sample load generator, secrets redaction tips, and a template prometheus-style output for latencies.
[08:21] Sofia: Great. Can you recap next steps?
[08:24] Lena: Sure — 1) I'll email the hosted vs dedicated pricing + quickstart playbook + SOC2/KMS docs by 2026-09-01. 2) Jon will schedule a 2-hour benchmark window and share the runbook; Jon also to produce a baseline latency test. 3) Priya to share anonymized 10k query sample and QPS targets by 2026-08-31. 4) We'll reconvene after benchmark (week of 2026-09-07).
[08:50] Amir: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[08:54] Priya: One last — are there any sample cost estimates for embedding-heavy workloads using quantization?
[08:59] Jon: We'll include an embedding cost model in the sheet. Quantization typically reduces token compute by 2–3x depending on model and hardware. We'll show scenarios.
[09:12] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and the runbook. Look forward to the benchmark.
[09:18] Amir: Thanks — appreciate it.

Meeting end: ~42m

Notes about transcript: minor transcription artifacts — names sometimes merged, and exact timings are approximated. References to product names: Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Optimize, KV cache, SS O (occasionally mis-transcribed), KMS/HSM.
